name: Shiftly
tagline: Scheduling software for shift-based teams: build rosters, track availability, publish shifts to staff.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core of any shift scheduler is a week grid, a list of people, and arithmetic: who is available, who is over their hours, who is double booked. That part an agent will hand you in a session, and for a single small team it is genuinely enough. The part that does not come free is everyone else in the building: staff need to see their shifts on a phone, request swaps, get notified when the roster changes, and none of that survives a localhost build. Add labor rules, overtime math, and payroll or POS export and the gap widens fast. Build it if you are the only one who ever opens it, and expect to keep publishing rosters by screenshot.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you define employees, availability and shift templates, drag through a week grid to assign shifts, and get instant conflict and hours-overrun warnings plus CSV and ICS export.
requirements: Node 20 and a machine that stays on if anyone else needs to view it
A way to distribute the published roster: printing, CSV, or an ICS feed
Willingness to hand-enter staff, availability and pay rates
whatYouLose: A phone app or mobile web view your staff actually check
Notifications when the roster changes, so no SMS, push or email blasts
Self-service: shift swap requests, time-off requests, approval flows
Payroll, POS and time-clock integrations that turn a roster into paid hours
Compliance guardrails: break rules, overtime thresholds, minor work restrictions, audit trail
moatNotes: The scheduler is the easy half. The moat is being the app the whole staff already has installed and the thing payroll reads from.
whyPeopleStillPay: Scheduling is only half a product, the other half is distribution. A manager can plan a week in a spreadsheet, what they cannot do is guarantee that twenty part-timers saw the change, acknowledged it, and got paid for the right hours. Paid tools carry the notification plumbing, the staff-side app, the swap approvals, and the export that reconciles with payroll, and they carry the blame when hours are wrong. Once a team's availability, rates and six months of history live in it, moving is a project nobody volunteers for.
notes: Fine as a personal rostering tool, weak the second a second human needs to read it.
prompt:
Build a local-first shift scheduling app for one small team. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable: Next.js 14 App Router with TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3 with plain SQL migrations in /db. Single process, runs with `npm run dev` on localhost. No ORM, no auth provider, no external APIs.

Data model:
- employees: id, name, role, hourly_rate, max_hours_per_week, color
- availability: employee_id, weekday (0-6), start_time, end_time, kind ('available' | 'unavailable')
- time_off: employee_id, start_date, end_date, note
- shift_templates: id, label, start_time, end_time, role, unpaid_break_minutes
- shifts: id, date, start_time, end_time, role, employee_id (nullable), template_id (nullable), notes, published (bool)

UI:
- Week view as the home page: days across the top, employees down the side, shift blocks in cells, arrow keys or buttons to move between weeks.
- Click an empty cell to create a shift from a template or by hand; click a shift to reassign, edit times, or delete. Drag and drop is optional, keyboard and click must work.
- Unassigned shifts sit in an 'open shifts' row at the top.
- A right sidebar showing, per employee for the visible week: scheduled hours, hours vs max, estimated labor cost.
- A warnings panel that recomputes on every change: double bookings, shifts outside declared availability, shifts during time off, over max weekly hours, under 8 hours rest between consecutive shifts, role mismatch.
- Copy-previous-week button that duplicates all shifts forward.
- Employees, templates and availability managed on simple CRUD pages.

Export:
- CSV of the visible week: date, employee, start, end, paid hours, cost.
- Printable roster view at /print/[weekStart], one page, no chrome.
- Read-only ICS feed at /api/ics/[employeeId] so a person can subscribe to their own shifts.

Explicitly out of scope: mobile apps, push or SMS notifications, swap and time-off request workflows, payroll integrations, multi-location, multi-tenant, labor-law compliance logic beyond the warnings listed above.

Seed the database with 6 employees, 4 templates and one filled week so the app is not empty on first run. Put DB_PATH and any config in .env with a committed .env.example. Write a README with setup, the data model, and a blunt 'what this does not do' section.
